description: Shared by the CLI approver and the web approver: both must head a request with the same text. Each case gives a wire action surface and syntactic substrate. `headline` is the CLI's Action line; `heading` is what the human decides on (the CLI's Deciding on line and the web card heading); they differ only when a command's raw and argv diverge, where the heading is the hash-bound argv. Expected values are written by hand from the rule in docs/threat-model.md R3 (the headline paragraph) and the Decision on issue #321, never from either renderer's output. On a tool surface (mcp_tool_call, agent_tool_call) naming a tool or a server, the tool identity wins: `server :: tool`, the tool alone, or `server :: (tool missing)` when there is no tool. Each half of the identity is shown bare only when it is printable ASCII with no `::` and no character that quotes a command token; otherwise it is single-quoted, so two different server/tool splits never render alike. The caller's raw is then shown as `description` (the CLI's Description line, the web plaintext's `description:` row), and a hash-bound bin/argv sets `tool_command_form` (both approvers warn that the call also carries a command). Otherwise, whatever the surface: a file edit's diff_summary, else `operation paths`; then raw; then the command bin/argv reconstruct to; then `operation paths`; then the compact params JSON; then the no-fields wording. `description` and `tool_command_form` are absent when they don't apply. `distinct_from` names another case that must render differently from this one. Tokens and list items are quoted as in raw-argv-divergence.json.
